parameters.jsCode: const body=$input.first().json.body;const required=['cohorts'];const missing=required.filter(f=>!body[f]);if(missing.length)return[{json:{valid:false,error:'Missing: '+missing.join(', ')}}];const cohorts=Array.isArray(body.cohorts)?body.cohorts:[];if(cohorts.length===0)return[{json:{valid:false,error:'cohorts must be non-empty'}}];const formatted=cohorts.slice(0,24).map((c,i)=>({label:(c.label||'Cohort '+(i+1)).trim(),startingCustomers:parseInt(c.starting_customers)||0,retentionByPeriod:Array.isArray(c.retention_by_period)?c.retention_by_period.map(v=>parseFloat(v)):[],segment:c.segment||'',acquisitionChannel:c.acquisition_channel||''}));const periodCount=Math.max(...formatted.map(c=>c.retentionByPeriod.length),0);return[{json:{valid:true,productName:(body.product_name||'').trim(),periodType:body.period_type||'month',cohorts:formatted,cohortCount:formatted.length,periodCount,businessContext:(body.business_context||'').slice(0,400),replyEmail:body.reply_email||null}}];

values.content: You analyze customer retention cohort data. Good cohort analysis identifies whether retention is improving or declining across newer vs older cohorts, distinguishes between the curve flattening (good — indicates a stable core) vs continuing to decay (concerning), spots segment or channel differences that explain patterns, and translates retention math into business implications. Always respond in valid JSON only.
